Apple recently replaced a billboard in Milan showing a young child holding an iPhone, as part of its latest "Relax, it's iPhone" advertising campaign. Here are the details.

Apple removes controversial billboard in Italy

A few days ago, Italy's child rights watchdog, the Autorità Garante per l'Infanzia e l'Adolescenza (AGIA), condemned Apple for depicting young children holding iPhones in its "Relax, it's iPhone" advertising campaign.

The campaign primarily promotes the iPhone's durability and sturdiness, featuring scenarios in which the iPhone gets wet, dropped, or otherwise used in ways that could potentially damage the device. Examples include taking photos in heavy rain, placing the iPhone on the edge of a bathtub to watch videos, a dog carrying the iPhone in its mouth, or a young child clumsily gripping the device.

After a billboard depicting the latter scenario was erected on Via Melchiorre Gioia in Milan, AGIA received a letter from a concerned individual stating that the advertisement normalised the practice of using devices as an "electronic nanny".

AGIA agreed with this view and referred the matter to AGCOM, Italy's communications regulator, AGCM, the Italian competition authority, as well as IAP, the country's advertising industry self-regulatory body, "for appropriate review and any necessary action".

According to Prima Comunicazione and Repubblica Milano, Apple has removed the controversial billboard and replaced it with one promoting the iPhone's "Find My" feature.

Apple has not publicly responded to the controversy, but the company's swift response demonstrates that it takes outside criticism seriously, even when the intended message of durability clashed with how it was interpreted.

What are your thoughts on this controversy? Feel free to share your views in the comments section.
